evidenceAudit.scope: Adult preventive care in Saudi primary care, including age- and risk-based blood-pressure, metabolic, cancer, osteoporosis and abdominal-aortic-aneurysm screening. The Saudi PHA 2023 guideline was checked against current opened USPSTF recommendations where newer recommendations differ.
findings: The Saudi PHA guideline is the local organising source and adapts international recommendations for Saudi primary care.
Screening eligibility and interval depend on age, sex, smoking exposure, body-mass index and other risk factors.
An abnormal screening result requires the named confirmatory or diagnostic pathway; screening alone does not establish every diagnosis.
The 2024 USPSTF breast-screening interval differs from the 2023 Saudi recommendation and is displayed separately.
unverifiedSections: The opened Saudi PHA guideline states that it should be updated every 2 years; no later official Saudi edition was located during this run.
Cervical-screening and adult-immunisation schedules were not made actionable because no post-2023 Saudi update was reconciled during this run.
Laboratory and radiology reference intervals remain service-specific.
No medicine regimen is prescribed in this preventive-examination topic; SFDA medicine-register verification is therefore not applicable.
Local referral capacity and programme-specific booking rules require clinician confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Periodic health examination is a structured preventive-care process for people who may have no symptoms. It applies screening only when the expected benefit exceeds harm, then closes the loop on abnormal results.
keyMechanisms: Age, sex, smoking exposure, body-mass index and comorbidity change baseline risk and therefore screening eligibility.
Repeated or confirmatory measurement reduces misclassification from a single abnormal screening result.
Defined screening intervals aim to detect selected disease before symptoms while limiting unnecessary intervention.
A positive screen changes the pathway from prevention to diagnostic confirmation and condition-specific care.

symptoms: Usually an asymptomatic attendance for preventive review.
A symptom disclosed during the visit moves that problem from screening to a diagnostic assessment.
physicalSigns: Blood pressure measured with a validated clinical method.
Body-mass index and waist circumference recorded at the recommended interval.
In older adults, fall history and mobility performance may identify a need for a falls pathway.
redFlags: Any acute symptom or unstable clinical finding: stop routine screening and use the relevant urgent diagnostic pathway.
Any abnormal screen without a named owner and diagnostic follow-up plan: resolve before closing the encounter.
precipitants: Age and sex determine eligibility for several cancer, osteoporosis and aneurysm screening programmes.
Smoking exposure determines lung-cancer and abdominal-aortic-aneurysm screening eligibility.
Body-mass index and metabolic risk factors alter diabetes-screening eligibility.
Prior screening date and result determine whether a test is due or requires diagnostic follow-up.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: No related symptoms; the person meets an age- or risk-based screening criterion.
Symptoms or abnormal examination findings require diagnostic testing rather than a screening interval.
A confirmed diagnosis requires its governed chronic-care or treatment pathway rather than screening thresholds.
The screening test is positive or abnormal, but the condition has not yet been confirmed.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: All adults aged 18 years or older; annually from age 40 years or with increased risk, otherwise every 3-5 years after a prior normal reading.
Fasting glucose, HbA1c or random blood sugar from age 35 years every 3 years; also screen adults with BMI 25 kg/m² or higher plus a listed risk factor.
Women aged 40-69 years: mammography every 1-2 years; evidence is insufficient for routine screening from age 75 years.
Adults aged 45-75 years; use yearly FIT or gFOBT, flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years, or colonoscopy every 10 years.

Annual low-dose CT for adults aged 50-80 years with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years; stop after 15 years without smoking or when health or treatment preference precludes curative surgery.
One-time ultrasonography for men aged 65-75 years who have ever smoked.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Screen all adults; select the interval by age and hypertension risk.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: An elevated clinic reading requires measurement outside the clinical setting before treatment is started.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Screen annually from age 40 years or with high-normal blood pressure, overweight or obesity. Screen every 3-5 years at ages 18-39 when risk is low and the prior reading was normal.
ruleIn.normalValue: Prior normal blood pressure; use the governed hypertension pathway for numeric diagnostic thresholds and confirmation.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Measure adults aged over 18 years every 2 years.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: BMI of 25 kg/m² or higher changes diabetes-screening eligibility; BMI of 30 kg/m² or higher is the Saudi threshold for offering or referring to intensive multicomponent behavioural intervention.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Record both measures and use them with age and risk factors rather than as a stand-alone diagnosis.
ruleIn.normalValue: BMI below 25 kg/m² is below the PHA overweight threshold used in the diabetes-screening rule; interpret waist circumference with the applicable local standard.

ruleIn.testName: Fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c or random blood sugar
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Screen from age 35 years every 3 years and apply the Saudi BMI-plus-risk-factor rule.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: A result in the prediabetes or diabetes range requires repeat or condition-specific diagnostic assessment.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: The USPSTF diagnostic ranges are fasting plasma glucose 100-125 mg/dL or HbA1c 5.7%-6.4% for prediabetes, and fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL or higher or HbA1c 6.5% or higher for diabetes; confirm diagnosis according to the diabetes pathway.
ruleIn.normalValue: Fasting plasma glucose below 100 mg/dL and HbA1c below 5.7% under the opened USPSTF ranges; local laboratory ranges apply.

ruleIn.targetCondition: Preclinical colorectal cancer or advanced adenoma
ruleIn.expectedFinding: A positive FIT or gFOBT, or an abnormal endoscopic result, requires diagnostic follow-up.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Choose one supported strategy: FIT or gFOBT yearly, flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years, or colonoscopy every 10 years. A positive non-colonoscopy test requires timely colonoscopy.
ruleIn.normalValue: Negative stool test at the stated interval or no clinically significant lesion on endoscopy; symptoms require diagnostic assessment irrespective of screening status.

ruleOut.testName: Diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive non-colonoscopy screen
ruleOut.modalityTarget: Positive FIT, positive gFOBT or another abnormal non-colonoscopy colorectal screen.
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Colonoscopy confirms or excludes a clinically significant colorectal lesion and directs pathology or treatment.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Do not repeat a positive stool screen as a substitute for diagnostic colonoscopy; arrange timely completion and track the result.
ruleOut.normalValue: No clinically significant lesion on diagnostic colonoscopy; subsequent interval is set by the endoscopy report and risk pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm that this is a preventive encounter
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At the start of the visit
actions: Record age, sex, smoking exposure, body-mass index, relevant comorbidity, prior screening dates and results.
Move any symptom or unstable finding to the relevant diagnostic or urgent pathway.
Identify every prior abnormal screen that still lacks diagnostic closure.

clinicalManagement.title: Complete due core measurements
actions: Measure blood pressure and select the next interval: annually from age 40 years or with increased risk; every 3-5 years at ages 18-39 when low risk with a prior normal reading.
Measure BMI and waist circumference every 2 years in adults aged over 18 years.
Offer glucose testing from age 35 years every 3 years and apply the Saudi BMI-plus-risk-factor rule.

clinicalManagement.title: Offer only eligible screening
clinicalManagement.timeframe: During the visit or booked preventive appointment
actions: Use the age, sex, smoking and risk criteria in the investigation table before ordering breast, colorectal, lung, osteoporosis or aneurysm screening.
Explain the expected next step before the test, including diagnostic follow-up after an abnormal result.
Document the Saudi recommendation and any current international difference used in shared decision making.

branches.condition: Screen is not yet due or eligibility is not met
actions: Record the reason and the next review date; do not order the test as routine screening.

branches.condition: Screen is due and the person accepts
actions: Place the order and name the clinician or service responsible for reviewing the result.

clinicalManagement.title: Act on every result
actions: Communicate the result and its meaning.
For an elevated blood-pressure screen, obtain out-of-office confirmation before treatment.
For a positive non-colonoscopy colorectal screen, arrange timely diagnostic colonoscopy.
Send other abnormal results to the matching diagnostic or specialty pathway and track completion.

clinicalManagement.title: Set the recall and responsibility plan
actions: Record completed, deferred and declined screening decisions.
Set the next due date for each selected intervention.
Name the responsible clinician or service for every pending test, referral and abnormal result.

medicationPlan.note: This topic selects and closes preventive screening. It does not prescribe preventive medicines. Use the governed condition-specific pathway when medication is indicated.

guidelineComparison.title: Opened Saudi and USPSTF screening recommendations

values: Women aged 40-69 years every 1-2 years; insufficient evidence from age 75 years.
Women aged 40-74 years every 2 years; insufficient evidence from age 75 years (2024).
Start at age 35 years every 3 years; also screen adults with BMI at least 25 kg/m² plus a listed risk factor.
Adults aged 35-70 years with overweight or obesity; screening every 3 years may be reasonable after a normal result (2021).
Offer from age 45 years through age 75 years using the listed stool or endoscopic intervals.
Screen ages 45-75 years; selectively offer at ages 76-85 years according to health, prior screening and preference (2021).

guidelineComparison.note: Use the Saudi PHA pathway as the local default. Record the source and shared decision when a newer international recommendation differs; clinician governance is required before adopting a different local interval.

teaching.scope: Adult periodic health examination in Saudi primary care.
learningObjectives: Separate asymptomatic screening from symptom-led diagnostic assessment.
Apply age, sex, smoking and metabolic-risk eligibility before ordering a screening test.
Close every abnormal screening result through the named diagnostic pathway.
Explain the breast-screening and diabetes-population differences between the opened Saudi and current USPSTF sources.
pitfalls: Ordering a screening test for a symptomatic problem instead of starting diagnostic assessment.
Repeating a positive stool test instead of arranging diagnostic colonoscopy.
Applying a screening interval without checking the last result and current eligibility.
Merging different Saudi and USPSTF age ranges into a new unsupported range.
Closing the encounter without assigning ownership for pending results.
keyPoints: Screening is risk- and interval-based; more testing is not automatically better.
The local Saudi guideline remains the organising source while differences are shown explicitly.
A screening programme is incomplete until abnormal results receive diagnostic follow-up.

patientEducation: Explain why each selected test is due and what will happen after a normal or abnormal result.
Explain that symptoms require diagnostic assessment even when a screening test was recently normal.
Use shared decision making when the Saudi and current international recommendations differ.
lifestyleAndDiet: Offer smoking-cessation support to people who smoke.
For BMI of 30 kg/m² or higher, offer or refer to an intensive multicomponent behavioural intervention.
Match nutrition and physical-activity advice to the person's measured risk and condition-specific pathway.
mdtReferrals: Primary-care preventive-care coordinator for recall and result tracking.
Diagnostic breast, colorectal, lung, osteoporosis or vascular service after an abnormal relevant screen.
Diabetes or hypertension pathway after confirmatory testing.
Behavioural support service for smoking cessation or obesity intervention.
dischargeCriteria: No acute symptom or unstable finding remains in the preventive pathway.
Eligibility, completed tests, declined tests and next due dates are documented.
Every pending or abnormal result has a named owner and follow-up route.
The person knows when and how results will be communicated.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: The ordering primary-care clinician reviews each result when available and moves abnormal results to the named diagnostic pathway. The preventive-care coordinator maintains the recall dates defined in the investigation table and rechecks eligibility when age, smoking exposure, body-mass index, health status or prior results change.
